there are two queues here, a DeltaFIFO used by the informer and a Workqueue, that is the one we are using for moving from Events to Workers https://github.com/kubernetes/sample-controller/blob/master/docs/controller-client-go.md

The Worqueue is the one that collapses and dedup https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/120799

The DeltaFIFO does not collapses, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/69c3b23abdbda53d14e14afc2af2bdfef23ac7b0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/delta_fifo.go#L80-L85 , the Informer passes all Deltas to the event handlers https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/69c3b23abdbda53d14e14afc2af2bdfef23ac7b0/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L434-L448

since this will add more load to the controller

OK, but the concern here is for the resource event handlers. I wrote a unit test on an experimental branch and saw that  it also collapses the events. 

> since this will add more load to the controller

I don't think that's necessarily true. The node queue still runs with one worker go-routine, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1e161f4dc4c36db9c54cac25fafcf20a6aa2643e/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L232 and the fact that we enqueue the update on the workqueue doesn't necessarily mean that we will actually sync the load balancer, that will be decided by  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1e161f4dc4c36db9c54cac25fafcf20a6aa2643e/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L710

And if the code is duplicate, I prefer to be conservative and wait until we have stable the predicates so we can revisit, doing many changes at the same time is super hard to debug later if something goes wrong https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/121116

I'm still sort of confused - the Informer UpdateFunc is called with old and new.  Are you saying that this might represent only the last of a series of updates, rather than the whole series?

e.g. given a node `Node{Field1: 1, Field2: 2}`, consider this sequence

T0: Create node A `Node{Field1: 1, Field2: 2}`
T1: call `AddFunc(Node{Field1: 1, Field2: 2})`
T2: Update node A `Node{Field1: 3, Field2: 2}`
T3: Update node A `Node{Field1: 3, Field2: 4}`
T4: call `UpdateFunc()`

Will UpdateFunc see old=`Node{Field1: 1, Field2: 2}` and new=`Node{Field1: 3, Field2: 4}` (covering both updates) or can it instead get old=`Node{Field1: 3, Field2: 2}` and new=`Node{Field1: 3, Field2: 4}` (covering only the last update)?

If it is the latter then a) Oh no!; and b) we shouldn't pass `old` at all - it's a lie!
Will it have a negative impact on performance if we enqueue all node event?

issue_context.title: [KCCM]: handle coalesced node updates in the service controller
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

On big clusters with a lot of churn, Node updates can be frequent. The service controller in the Kubernetes cloud controller manager (KCCM) uses an edge-triggered resource watcher for what concerns handling the Update events, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L160-L176

This means that Node events which should trigger a sync (ex: the addition/removal of the label `exclude-from-load-balancer`) can be missed if multiple updates occur on the same object in a short amount of time. 

The `UpdateFunc` doc bloc even explicitly warns about patterns such as the one described above, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L207-L212

This pattern has always been used in the KCCM, but I believe that since some Node conditions which used to trigger re-syncs have been removed since 1.26, the error can be triggered more often now. Specifically on < 1.26, the `NotReady` condition on the Node used to trigger a re-sync. This condition usually occurs when the Node stabilizes, sometime after its initial creation. This covered the existing issue.    

/sig network
/sig cloud-provider
/cc @aojea @thockin 


### What did you expect to happen?

All Node events should get enqueued. The Node controller will compare the current set of nodes in its informer cache to the last set of Nodes it synced, if a change is observed the load balancer is synced, see: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/cloud-provider/controllers/service/controller.go#L746-L751 - this shouldn't even lead to additional syncs because of this.  

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

This can be observed on upgrading clusters with a lot of Nodes and Services of `type: LoadBalancer`. Some Nodes might get excluded from the load balancer's backend, not because they should be excluded but because the update which should include it is missed. 

### Anything else we need to know?
